source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Watermelon Mosaic virus causes leaves to develop a mottled yellow-green mosaic pattern and to become curled, wrinkled, or deformed, with the whole plant often showing stunted growth. On fruit, the disease can cause ring-shaped or mottled discoloration patterns on the rind. The virus is spread from plant to plant primarily by aphids feeding on the crop.

Because it is caused by a virus, there is no direct chemical cure once a plant is infected; management instead focuses on controlling the aphid vector that transmits the disease (see aphid control) and on promptly removing and destroying visibly infected plants to reduce the source of further spread within the field. Using resistant varieties where available and keeping the crop free of aphid infestation are the main preventive measures.
